newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currencies to new lows, sterling rallies.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currencies to new lows, sterling rallies.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended sharply lower on technical momentum after the dollar reached key upside targets Monday and early Tuesday, some slumping to contract lows.

December marks, Swiss francs, and yen all hit contract lows early in the day amid active volume. Piqued interest in U.S. assets after a record Dow close on Monday set the tone overnight, and expectations for continued stock strength early Tuesday kept the pressure on currencies early.
Even as stocks failed to follow through on the upside, key currencies remained near their contract lows all session.
Meanwhile, December British pound rallied to a fresh contract high at $1.5890, hitting waves of buy stops amid good early volume.
Sterling options activity was brisk in afternoon trade, with several traders noting buying of about 2,500 March 1.52/1.60 strangles and selling of November 1.56/1.58 strangles.

Traders said fundamentals and technicals were converging in sterling. Firm oil prices, ideas the currency is a safe-haven for European Monetary Union, and propects for higher interest rates all buoyed the market, traders said.

Technically, weekly and monthly indicators turned positive for December sterling last week when it took out key resistance at $1.5712, the September 5 high, a technician said. That old top represents a sound floor for the market now, he added.

Another trader said December sterling could challenge the $1.60 upside target early on Wednesday, then scale back in a correction from recent gains. December sterling has posted new contract highs for three consecutive sessions.
Trade was very active in December Mexican peso as technical action dominated the market, traders said.
December peso slid to the lowest price since early September, helped by sellstops around $0.124000. The market later recovered to close in the top half of its range.
Volume was brisk in peso futures, with overall peso volume estimated by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange at 9,976 contracts.
"It's been a technical breakdown since Friday, and a swift bailout all the way down," an IMM trading desk manager said. Traders noted hefty-sized orders and big players on both sides of the market.

December yen settled down $0.000051 at $0.008987, marks closed down $0.0053 to $0.6516, Swiss francs dropped $0.0106 to $0.7932, Sterling rallied $0.0078 to end at $1.5876, Can dollar fell $0.0010 to $0.7409, Aussie dollar dropped $0.0010 to $0.7887, and peso closed flat at $0.124450. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
